question: European stainless-steel producers now face unfair competition and market distortions because of circumvention of restrictions on imports of stainless steel from Indonesia, which enters the European market via other countries such as Turkey, Taiwan and Vietnam.

Dumped imports of what is subsidised stainless steel result in artificially low prices on the EU market, leading to job losses and the postponing of essential investments by European producers. Despite the Commission’s efforts to date, the situation remains worrying.

Indirect imports from countries such as Türkiye, Taiwan and Vietnam remain high, meaning that anti-dumping measures are being circumvented and further disadvantaging European producers. Signals from the sector are of concern.

In line with the Antwerp Declaration, which calls for the use of all policy instruments to ensure a level playing field for European industry, the Commission should give consideration to further tangible measures to address circumvention of anti-dumping measures and effectively protect the European stainless-steel industry against continuing unfair competitive practices. 1.
Is this situation being monitored by the Commission at all times in order to precisely map circumvention of import restrictions via other third countries?
What measures is the Commission considering in order to put an end to these market distortive practices? Within what timeframe?
answer: All anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures on stainless steel exports from Indonesia are subject to special monitoring, as the Commission found an increased risk of circumvention in the investigations leading to these measures. The risks stem from product fungibility, a high number of exporters and marked differences between company-specific and country-wide residual duty rates.

Special monitoring secures the proper enforcement of measures by monitoring global trade flows and systematic exchanging information with the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) and Member States’ investigating authorities to detect any potential circumvention practices. The Commission also promptly follows up specific information received from the EU industry to ensure appropriate remedial action.

The Commission has recently taken several actions to address the circumvention of trade defence measures on stainless steel. In 2023, existing anti-dumping measures against Indonesia on stainless steel hot-rolled flat products were extended to Türkiye following an anti-circumvention investigation.

In the same year, the Commission initiated two investigations against Taiwan, Türkiye and Vietnam concerning the circumvention of the anti-dumping and countervailing measures on stainless-steel cold-rolled flat products from Indonesia. The publication of the Commission’s findings will take place before 11 May 2024.

The Commission remains ready and willing to continue using the anti-circumvention instrument rigorously, to ensure the effectiveness of existing trade defence measures to the full extent allowed by the World Trade Organisation law and the EU legislation.
